fields.text: Player B says no spies among A and F, so B must be truth-telling knight, meaning no spy in A or F. Player C says 'not at most 1 spy' among 5 players including F; only one spy exists, so C lies and is knave. Player D says B and C differ, which is true, so D is knight. Player E says A is not knight; if E lies, A is knight contradicting other clues, so E is knight, implying A is not knight (knave). F is the only remaining player for spy. Roles assigned accordingly.

Player A's statement is true if either at least two of A and B are knaves or A and B have the same role. Since A is knight (always true), at least one holds. Player B's statement denies 'at least 0 of A and F are spies' which is false since zero or more is true, so B lies, hence knave. Player C claims 'not at most 1 spy among five players'; since only one spy exists, this is false, so C lies, knave. Player D claims B and C differ; since B and C are both knaves, this is false; D lies or tells truth? D must be spy to satisfy only one spy. Player E denies A is knight; since A is knight, E's statement is false, so E lies. But only one spy allowed; so E must be knight telling truth. F's statement about at most 2 knights among C, D, E, F holds with the assignments. Thus roles assigned consistently.

Player B's statement is false only if there is at least one spy among A and F, implying one spy in A or F. Player C's statement is false, so more than one spy among A,B,C,E,F; only one spy total, so C is knave. Player D says B and C differ, which is true, so D is knight. E denies A is knight; if E is knight, A not knight. F's statement is true if at most two among C,D,E,F are knights; counting D and E as knights, F is knight. Thus, A is spy, B and C knaves, D,E,F knights.
